subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep audit treat installed plugin manifests above 1 MiB as unreadable, emit a warning, and continue scanning the plugin root without manifest-declared forced entries?
rationale: The implementation safely bounds the read, but the threshold deliberately defines how much manifest-driven coverage deep audit retains for unusually large valid manifests.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Keep the current cap because oversized manifests remain visible and the plugin root still receives the normal directory scan.

options.title: Revise bounded extraction
options.body: Select another cap or a bounded field-extraction approach if declared entries on normally skipped paths must remain covered.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the current cap because oversized manifests remain visible and the plugin root still receives the normal directory scan.
